rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas allows meat slaughtered by a Muslim without pronouncing God's name, reasoning that the Muslim himself bears one of God's names; al-Daraqutni's report supports an earlier mursal report.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إذا ذبح المسلم -ولم يذكر اسم الله فليأكل، فإن المسلم فيه اسم من أسماء الله

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Bayhaqi cites Aisha's report: people unsure whether newly Muslim meat providers invoked God's name were told to invoke it themselves and eat; he infers that requiring verified invocation would have prevented this permission.
rows.anchor: واحتج البيهقي أيضا بحديث عائشة، رضي الله عنها، المتقدم أن ناسا قالوا

rows.speaker: الإمام مالك، وأحمد بن حنبل، وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه، وإسحاق بن راهويه، وعلي، وابن عباس، وسعيد بن المسيب، وعطاء، وطاوس، والحسن البصري، وأبي مالك، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وجعفر بن محمد، وربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: This school holds that forgetting the basmala does not invalidate slaughter, while deliberate omission makes the meat unlawful.
rows.anchor: هذا هو المشهور من مذهب الإمام مالك، وأحمد بن حنبل، وبه يقول أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، وإسحاق بن راهويه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن المرغيناني
rows.claim: Al-Marghinani claims consensus before al-Shafi'i that deliberately omitting God's name is forbidden; Abu Yusuf and the jurists say a judge's contrary ruling validating sale is unenforceable.
rows.anchor: نقل الإمام أبو الحسن المرغيناني في كتابه "الهداية" الإجماع -قبل الشافعي على تحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls al-Marghinani's claimed consensus very strange because disagreement before al-Shafi'i was already reported.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله غريب جدا، وقد تقدم نقل الخلاف عمن قبل الشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says anyone who forbids meat from slaughter forgottenly departs from all authoritative scholars and contradicts a sound report from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو جعفر بن جرير: من حرم ذبيحة الناسي، فقد خرج من قول جميع الحجة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a Muslim's name suffices: if he forgets to invoke God while slaughtering, he should remember God's name and eat.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "المسلم يكفيه اسمه، إن نسي أن يسمي حين يذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report was mistakenly raised to the Prophet: Sa'id b. Mansur and al-Humaydi transmit it from Sufyan, adding Abu al-Sha'tha and stopping it at Ibn Abbas; this is more correct, as al-Bayhaqi and other hadith experts state.
rows.anchor: وهذا أصح، نص عليه البيهقي [وغيره من الحفاظ]

rows.speaker: الشعبي، ومحمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Sirin disapproved of meat when God's name was omitted forgetfully; early authorities often used disapproval to mean prohibition.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي، ومحمد بن سيرين، أنهما كرها متروك التسمية نسيانا، والسلف يطلقون الكراهية على التحريم كثيرا

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir's method does not count one or two dissenters against the majority as meaningful opposition, and so treats the majority position as consensus.
rows.anchor: من قاعدة ابن جرير أنه لا يعتبر قول الواحد ولا الاثنين مخالفا لقول الجمهور، فيعده إجماعا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When asked about mixed birds, some slaughtered with invocation and some with it forgotten, al-Hasan said to eat them all.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن: كله، كله. قال: وسألت محمد بن سيرين

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Asked about the same mixed birds, Ibn Sirin invoked the verse forbidding eating what was slaughtered without God's name, implying they should not all be eaten.
rows.anchor: قال: وسألت محمد بن سيرين فقال: قال الله [تعالى] (9)

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted through Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, Abu Dharr, Uqba b. Amir, and Abd Allah b. Amr says God has excused the community for error, forgetfulness, and coercion; Ibn Kathir says this proof needs scrutiny.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله وضع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asked about forgetting to invoke God at slaughter, and the Prophet replied, “God's name upon every Muslim”; Ibn Kathir grades this chain weak because Marwan b. Salim was weak and criticized.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says he treated this question separately, detailing the jurists' positions, their evidence, reasoning, objections, and counterarguments.
rows.anchor: وقد أفردت هذه المسألة على حدة، وذكرت مذاهب

rows.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that none of the verse's ruling was abrogated and that it remains operative in its intended sense.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: لم ينسخ منها شيء وهي محكمة فيما عنيت به. وعلى هذا قول عامة أهل العلم

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ikrima say the prohibition was abrogated by the permission for the food of the People of the Book in 5:5.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة والحسن البصري قالا قال الله: {فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Mak'hul says the prohibition was abrogated by 5:5, which declares good things and the food of the People of the Book lawful to Muslims.
rows.anchor: ثم نسخها الرب ورحم المسلمين فقال: {اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the permission for the food of the People of the Book does not conflict with prohibiting what was slaughtered without God's name; Ibn Kathir agrees and explains that early use of “abrogation” here means specification.
rows.anchor: والصواب أنه لا تعارض بين حل طعام أهل الكتاب، وبين تحريم ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir endorses Ibn Jarir's reconciliation, explaining that early authorities who spoke of abrogation meant that the rule was specified rather than cancelled.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله صحيح، ومن أطلق من السلف النسخ هاهنا فإنما أراد التخصيص

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: When told that al-Mukhtar claimed to receive revelation, Ibn Umar answered that he spoke truly and cited the verse about Satan inspiring his allies.
rows.anchor: قال رجل لابن عمر: أن المختار يزعم أنه يوحى إليه؟ قال: صدق، وتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that there are two kinds of revelation: God's revelation to Muhammad and Satan's inspiration to its allies, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: هما وحيان، وحي الله، ووحي الشيطان

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr reports that Jews disputed with the Prophet, asking why Muslims ate what they slaughtered but not what God killed; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: خاصمت اليهود النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا: نأكل مما قتلنا، ولا نأكل مما قتل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Jews asked the Prophet why Muslims ate what they slaughtered but not what God killed; it is sent from Sa'id b. Jubayr and also transmitted connected from Ibn Abbas, with parallel routes from Ibn Jarir and al-Bazzar.
rows.anchor: جاءت اليهود إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: نأكل مما قتلنا ولا نأكل مما قتل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir questions the report because Jews did not regard carrion as lawful, the surah is Meccan, and al-Tirmidhi's version calls it a hasan gharib report also transmitted mursal from Sa'id b. Jubayr.
rows.anchor: وهذا فيه نظر من وجوه ثلاثة: أحدها: أن اليهود لا يرون إباحة الميتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Persia urged Quraysh to challenge Muhammad: why was what God supposedly killed with a golden sword (carrion) forbidden while their own slaughter was lawful? The verse identifies Persian satans and Qurayshi allies.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت {ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه} أرسلت فارس إلى قريش: أن خاصموا محمدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satanic allies argued that what God killed should not be eaten while what people slaughtered should; the verse came down in response.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم} يقولون: ما ذبح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Ibn Abbas report transmitted without the Jewish setting is the preserved version; the route cited by Ibn Majah and Ibn Abi Hatim is sound.
rows.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح. ورواه ابن جرير من طرق متعددة، عن ابن عباس، وليس فيه ذكر اليهود، فهذا هو المحفوظ

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that Quraysh corresponded with Persia, whose challenge about eating carrion troubled some Muslims; God revealed this verse and 6:112 in response.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن دينار، عن عكرمة: إن مشركي قريش كاتبوا فارس على الروم، وكاتبتهم فارس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says polytheists challenged believers for eating what they slaughtered while refusing what God killed; God warned that obeying them and eating carrion would be associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي في تفسير هذه الآية: إن المشركين قالوا للمؤمنين: كيف تزعمون أنكم تتبعون مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد، والضحاك، وغير واحد من علماء السلف
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and other early scholars likewise explain the warning as a response to the polytheists' argument for eating carrion.
rows.anchor: وهكذا قاله مجاهد، والضحاك، وغير واحد من علماء السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying the polytheists means preferring another's rule to God's command and law, which Ibn Kathir identifies as shirk; he links this to 9:31, where people take rabbis, monks, and the Messiah as lords.
rows.anchor: حيث عدلتم عن أمر الله لكم وشرعه إلى قول غيره، فقدمتم عليه غيره فهذا هو الشرك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report from Adi b. Hatim, the Prophet explains that people worshipped religious authorities by following them when they made the forbidden lawful and the lawful forbidden.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم أنه قال: يا رسول الله، ما عبدوهم، فقال: "بل إنهم أحلوا لهم الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Muhammad, the master of messengers, to report the favor of guidance to a straight path, free from crookedness or deviation; “a sound religion” means upright and established.
rows.anchor: آمرا نبيه (8) صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد المرسلين أن يخبر بما أنعم الله به عليه من الهداية إلى صراطه المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of Abraham's faith as pure is linked to 2:130, 22:78, and 16:120–123; these passages describe Abraham's upright monotheism and command Muhammad to follow it.
rows.anchor: {ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين} كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being commanded to follow Abraham's pure faith does not make Abraham more complete than Muhammad: Muhammad fulfilled it fully, surpassed all predecessors in this, and is the final prophet and master of Adam's children, whose praised station even Abraham approaches with awe.
rows.anchor: أمر باتباع ملة إبراهيم الحنيفية أن يكون إبراهيم أكمل منه فيها

rows.speaker: أبوه
rows.claim: Ubayy reports a morning formula affirming Islam, the word of sincerity, Muhammad's religion, and the religion of Abraham, upright and not among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبزى، عن أبيه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصبح قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked which religion God loves most, the Prophet replied: tolerant, upright monotheism.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الأديان أحب إلى الله؟ قال: "الحنيفية السمحة"

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet's opening prayer after the takbir recited the orientation to the Creator in 6:79 and the declaration that prayer, sacrifice, life, and death belong to God alone in 6:162–163; Muslim recorded the full report in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا كبر استفتح، ثم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God granted Iblis respite until resurrection, Iblis defiantly vowed to sit across the straight path of God's servants, Adam's descendants, and turn them away from truth and salvation so they would not worship or affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: أخذ في المعاندة والتمرد، فقال: {فبما أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets Iblis's phrase as “because You misled me.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كما أضللتني

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other authorities interpret the phrase as “because You destroyed me,” then describe Iblis blocking God's servants on the path of truth and salvation.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: كما أهلكتني لأقعدن لعبادك

rows.speaker: بعض النحاة
rows.claim: Some grammarians take the prefixed ba as an oath: “By Your leading me astray, I will sit in wait for them.”
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحاة: الباء هاهنا قسمية، كأنه يقول: فبإغوائك إياي لأقعدن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the straight path means the truth.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: {صراطك المستقيم} يعني: الحق.

rows.speaker: محمد بن سوقة، عن عون بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Muhammad b. Suqa, reporting from Awn b. Abd Allah, interprets the straight path as the road to Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد (2) بن سوقة، عن عون بن عبد الله: يعني طريق مكة.

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the broader interpretation that the straight path encompasses all these meanings; Ibn Kathir supports it with a report about Satan blocking people on life's paths.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير: والصحيح أن الصراط المستقيم أعم من ذلك [كله]

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that Satan waits on the human paths of Islam, migration, and jihad, tempting people to abandon each; those who resist and die, are killed, drown, or fall from a mount are promised Paradise by God.
rows.anchor: عن سبرة بن أبي فاكه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن الشيطان قعد لابن آدم بطرقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the directions as Satan sowing doubts about the afterlife from the front, enticing through worldly life from behind, confusing religion from the right, and making sins desirable from the left.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم} أشككهم في آخرتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن طلحة والعوفي
rows.claim: In another interpretation, Ibn Abbas says the front is worldly life, the rear is the afterlife, the right is good deeds, and the left is sins.
rows.anchor: وقال [علي] (12) بن طلحة -في رواية -والعوفي، كلاهما عن ابن عباس: أما {من بين أيديهم} فمن قبل دنياهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Satan denies resurrection and the Garden and Fire from the front, beautifies worldly life behind, diverts from good deeds on the right, and decorates evil and sins on the left.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: أتاهم {من بين أيديهم} فأخبرهم أنه (13) لا بعث ولا جنة ولا نار

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي، والحكم بن عتيبة، والسدي، وابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hakam b. Utayba, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir also transmit the front as worldly life and the rear as the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وكذا روي عن إبراهيم النخعي، والحكم بن عتيبة (2) والسدي، وابن جرير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the front and right are directions people can see, while the rear and left are directions they cannot see.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: "من بين أيديهم وعن أيمانهم": حيث يبصرون

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the comprehensive sense: Satan obstructs every path of good and makes every path of evil attractive.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد جميع طرق الخير والشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that Satan did not approach from above because mercy descends from above.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكم بن أبان، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “most of them ungrateful” as meaning most are not monotheists.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين} قال: موحدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Iblis's boast was a conjecture that proved true in practice and links it to 34:20–21: most followed him except believers, while he had no authority over them, distinguishing belief from doubt about the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقد وافق في هذا الواقع، كما قال تعالى: {ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's prayer for forgiveness and well-being in religion, worldly life, family, and wealth, and for protection from every direction and from being seized from below; al-Bazzar alone transmits it and grades it hasan.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet regularly recited morning and evening prayers for well-being, concealment of vulnerabilities, security from fear, and protection in every direction; Waki' explains the refuge from below as protection from being swallowed by the earth, and al-Hakim grades the chain sound.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمر يقول: لم يكن رسول الله يدع هؤلاء الدعوات حين يصبح وحين يمسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the humiliation of the people of the Fire as they beg the people of the Garden for drink and food and are denied.
rows.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن ذلة أهل النار وسؤالهم أهل الجنة من شرابهم وطعامهم، وأنهم لا يجابون إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets what God provided as food.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: {ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله}

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Zayd b. Aslam says the people of the Fire ask the people of the Garden for both food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: يستطعمونهم ويستسقونهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr describes a man calling his father or brother because he is burning and begging for water; when the Gardeners are told to answer, they reply that both are forbidden to unbelievers. A parallel report from Sa'id via Ibn Abbas says the same.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في هذه الآية قال: ينادي الرجل أباه أو أخاه فيقول: قد احترقت، أفض

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Zayd b. Aslam identifies the forbidden food and drink as the Garden's food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: {إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين} يعني: طعام الجنة وشرابها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's judgment that water is the best charity, drawing on the people of the Fire's plea for water in this verse.
rows.anchor: فقال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أفضل الصدقة الماء، ألم تسمع إلى أهل النار

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: When Abu Talib was ill, people suggested that the Prophet might send him a cluster of fruit from Paradise to cure him; Abu Bakr replied that God had forbidden the Garden's food and drink to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر: إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are described as treating religion as amusement and play and being deceived by worldly life, which distracted them from the commanded work for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف تعالى الكافرين بما كانوا يعتمدونه في الدنيا من اتخاذهم الدين لهوا ولعبا، واغترارهم بالدنيا
